name: 4d-blog-engine
description: 4D Blog Engine — operationalizes the 4D AI Fluency Framework (Delegation, Description, Discernment, Diligence) for content production. v0.10.0 restructures the LinkedIn output of /blog-social to match how LinkedIn's algorithm actually treats posts vs. articles. The default LinkedIn artifact is now a Post + first-comment pair (replacing the old "teaser"): linkedin-post.md is the feed Post (1,300-2,500 chars sweet spot, 2,900 hard cap under LinkedIn's 3,000-char post-rejection ceiling) with zero outbound links in the body, and linkedin-first-comment.md is the companion service payload (fixed intro line + blog URL + only the 2-3 sources the Post text quotes inline). The long-form LinkedIn Article is now an optional separate selection rather than auto-paired with the Post — most pieces only need the Post + first-comment. scripts/social_score.py renames --type teaser to --type post (teaser kept as a deprecated alias for one cycle) and adds --type first-comment with a URL-required check (the comment payload is empty without sources) plus a markdown-link-syntax warning (LinkedIn comments render as plain text — use bare URLs). The first-comment file gets a deterministic-check-only scorecard (no 3-axis LLM scoring — it's a utilitarian payload, not voice prose). marketplace.json was bumped from 0.8.1 to 0.10.0 to catch a pre-existing sync drift with plugin.json. v0.9.0 closed the social-derivative ship-to-repo gap end-to-end: /blog-publish now auto-detects `<piece>/04-diligence/social/` and includes any LinkedIn / Twitter / Facebook source files (plus their scorecards) in the same commit as the post, under `<social-subfolder>/<slug>/` (default `content/blog/social/<slug>/`, configurable via auto-detection like POSTS/IMAGES/MEDIA subfolders). On the way into the repo, each social file's `source_blog:` frontmatter field is rewritten from the local archive path to the in-repo path of the published post, so downstream distribution automation reading from GitHub resolves cleanly. The rewrite is the only edit — scorecards copy verbatim. Detection is silent: if /blog-social hasn't been run for a piece, the social step is skipped without warning, and publish ships post + hero + media only (same behavior as pre-v0.9). The actual paste-and-post step on each platform stays manual, by design (whitepaper Diligence ethos). /blog-social now ends with a clear pointer at /blog-publish; /blog-publish's 'does NOT do' section clarifies it ships source files, not auto-posts. v0.8.1 removed the stale `user-invocable: false` flag from the blog-social SKILL.md frontmatter — the flag was inherited from the old linkedin-deriver skill (which was only called internally by the release-owner-gate) and was blocking Cowork from dispatching the `/blog-social` slash command, causing the slash picker to fuzzy-match `/social-content` instead. v0.8.0 renamed /blog-linkedin to /blog-social and expands it from LinkedIn-only to multi-platform: LinkedIn (article + teaser, existing behavior), Twitter/X (5-10 post thread with ≤280-char per-post hard cap, script-enforced), Facebook (single 300-500 char post with body-inline link). One voice profile with per-platform register shifts (Twitter compressed/declarative, Facebook warmer/conversational, LinkedIn professional). Social derivation is opt-in — release-owner-gate's STEP 6 no longer auto-invokes anything; after Phase 4 sign-off, the writer runs /blog-social explicitly and picks which platforms to derive via AskUserQuestion (multiSelect). Outputs land in <piece>/04-diligence/social/ with per-platform scorecards under <piece>/04-diligence/social/scorecards/. scripts/linkedin_score.py renamed to scripts/social_score.py with TYPE_BANDS extended for twitter-thread (per-post char check + thread structure check) and facebook-post (length band, hashtag cap of 2, body-link allowed). hook-library.md expanded with a per-platform formula-fit table mapping the six named formulas (Stat-Led, Question, Story, Contrarian, Bold Claim, Pattern Interrupt) to platform sweet spots, plus per-platform output contracts and fold/char-limit rules. v0.7.0 renamed all remaining bare-name commands to the blog-* prefix for full consistency. v0.6.1 hardened scripts/smart_quotes.py against the YAML-curly-quote class of bugs. v0.6.0 renamed /publish to /blog-publish. v0.5.7 closed the media-file gap end-to-end: /blog-init creates Posts/, drafts/, and drafts/blog-media/ at setup; /blog-start scans the session's uploads/ folder and offers 'Start a new post from your uploads' as the top option; the /blog orchestrator's Phase 2 scans drafts/blog-media/ and asks for one-line captions per file; /blog-publish parses the YAML media: array, copies files to the publishing repo's public/blog-media/, and includes them in one commit alongside the post and hero. The writer drops files into chat, types captions when asked, says 'go' once, clicks Push origin in GitHub Desktop. No PAT, no API token, no MCP-server auth config. Silent .git/index.lock recovery if GitHub Desktop's file-watcher races the commit. Byte-identical republishes silently bump dateModified so the rebuild fires once pushed. v0.5.2 introduced the local drafts/ convention. v0.5.0 rewrote /blog-publish end-to-end with vendored smart_quotes.py. v0.4.0 added /blog-voice (multi-voice supported) and unhardcoded all preset-voice references. v0.3.x stripped backend infrastructure out of the writer-facing setup. v0.2.0 added the lifecycle commands. Pipeline: takes a base document and an angle question; runs a 30-day discourse sweep across reddit, X, Hacker News, Substack, Facebook, Quora, podcasts, and academic sources; layers a /council:deliberate synthesis pass; builds a verified bibliography with AI-generated abstracts; drafts the blog post in the writer's voice using the research-pipeline content-writer; runs a two-tier anti-AI-slop pass (deterministic linter + LLM structural review with a second-pass audit); ships through a nonce-bound Release Owner Gate scoring against a 100-point rubric. On a clean gate, produces a publication-ready blog post. The writer opts in to multi-platform social derivation via /blog-social. Trigger phrases: 'write a blog post from this document', 'derive a blog from this whitepaper', 'make a Twitter thread from this blog', 'write a Facebook post from my blog', '/4d-blog-engine', 'set up the blog plugin', 'publish this post', 'release-owner gate'. Implements the Release Owner Gate from MoxyWolf's 'Beyond the Prompt' whitepaper.
